params.head: Equal Care Across Finland: where is the gap?

scenes.cap: The gap, in one picture. Each county is an aggregate twin of the cancer pathway, built from public THL and Cancer Registry data. Red: a gap we can identify. Hatched: too few patients to judge.

caps: We replay history. Each month both models see only what had been published by then.
Model 3 is the strategy's own monitoring: an annual review of figures two years old. Model 4 re-targets the same three pilot slots every month.
Referral gaps move between counties. Model 4 reaches 51% of gap-months; Model 3 reaches 20%. Same lever, same budget.
Goal 3, treatment start. The public proxy is the oncology queue, in days of referral inflow.
Here the gaps are chronic. Model 4 reaches 60%, Model 3 56%: a tie. Faster monitoring does not help where the gap never moves.
Diagnosis: the endoscopy queue. 38% against 34%, also a tie.

params.head: Scoreboard: every success factor of the strategy

scenes.cap: The scoreboard lists every success factor. Model 4 wins one, ties two. Survival, mortality and stage are not estimated: no public county data. The twin missed the 2020 pandemic dip and only ties the last-value baseline on half the signals. We show that.

The action for one county. Päijät-Häme: 61% of patients waiting for a first specialist assessment have waited over 90 days; nationally 17%. Standardised referral criteria and a fast track, roadmap measure 2.5.2, owner named, evidence cited, effect not yet estimated, checked monthly.
